t:
Within the end strengths prescribed in section 411(a), the reserve components of the Armed Forces are authorized, as of September 30, 2018, the following number of Reserves to be serving on full-time active duty or full-time duty, in the case of members of the National Guard, for the purpose of organizing, administering, recruiting, instructing, or training the reserve components:
    (1) The Army National Guard of the United States, 30,155. 
    (2) The Army Reserve, 16,261. 
    (3) The Navy Reserve, 10,101. 
    (4) The Marine Corps Reserve, 2,261. 
    (5) The Air National Guard of the United States, 16,260. 
    (6) The Air Force Reserve, 3,588.

fable.w: This section only sets authorized end strengths for reserve personnel on full-time duty. The tempting reading is that the National Guard has state ties, but the section provides no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. It is a personnel authorization with no outside-party role in any federal decision.
fable.s: the reserve components of the Armed Forces are authorized, as of September 30, 2018, the following number of Reserves to be serving on full-time active duty

opus.w: This section only sets the authorized number of full-time reserve personnel in each component. The mention of the National Guard might suggest state involvement, but the section never asks states, the public or any other outside party to be consulted or to take part in a federal decision. It also creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue.
opus.s: the reserve components of the Armed Forces are authorized, as of September 30, 2018, the following number of Reserves to be serving on full-time active duty

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes specific numbers of reserve personnel for various branches of the military. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. The activities mentioned (organizing, administering, recruiting, instructing, training) are internal military operations, not participatory processes involving non-federal actors in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Within the end strengths prescribed in section 411(a), the reserve components of the Armed Forces are authorized, as of September 30, 2018, the following number of Reserves to be serving on full-time active duty or full-time duty...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "recruiting" or "training" involves interaction with the public (potential recruits or trainees). However, these are operational activities of the military, not a process where outside parties consult with or participate in a federal decision-making process. The section merely sets numerical limits for personnel.
